# Tests that skip at CELERIS_MAX_IOURING_TIER=base on purpose, for .github/scripts/base-tier-tally.sh
# (celeris#890 item 87): the full test or subtest name, then why. A name covers its own
# subtests. Measured on the run of the job iouring-base-tier cited in the pull request:
# 107 top-level tests passed, 3 skipped at the top level, 19 SKIP lines in all (and
# 117 passed with 46 SKIP lines once main had brought in nine more tests of the kind below).
min-pass 100

# The probes of the tests that gate their io_uring arms (c714ProbeIOUring,
# keptProbeIOUring, h2_handler_return_889's) call io_uring "usable" only at the high
# tier with provided buffers, so with the cap their io_uring and adaptive arms skip with
# "io_uring tier=base kernel=...: no usable io_uring". The std and epoll arms of the
# same tests run. A new test of this kind joins them without an edit here, because the
# entry names the arms, not the tests (run 40419578127 met nine new ones that a merge
# with main brought in: the TestH1Unclosed...889 family); the log must say tier=base
# under the skipped arm, so an arm that skips for another reason still fails the step.
pattern:^.+/(io_uring|adaptive|adaptive-iouring)$ the io_uring, adaptive and adaptive-iouring arms of probe-gated tests

# Tier base has no multishot recv, and these two tests are about it.
TestHijackCopiesRequestValuesUnderMultishotRecv tier base has no multishot recv
TestMultishotRingSurvivesHijacks tier base has no multishot recv

# Its probe (keptProbeIOUring) calls io_uring usable only at the high tier: "no usable io_uring".
TestServerAsyncRouteDetachThenGoexitOnIOUring no usable io_uring at the base tier
